title: A Worm Up to 10 Feet Long Ambushes Fish From the Sand

scenes.text: This worm hides in the sand and snaps fish in half.
It's called the bobbit worm, and it can grow up to ten feet long.
It buries its body in the seafloor with only its antennae sticking out.
When a fish swims close, it lunges out and strikes hard enough to cleave it in half.
Then it drags the prey into its burrow and injects a toxin that digests it.
So the next time you see sand underwater, remember what might be hiding in it.
